requirements.heading: UTF-8 Address Type
requirements.text: An SMTP [RFC5321] server that advertises both the SMTPUTF8 extension [RFC6531] and the DSN extension [RFC3461] MUST accept a UTF-8 address type in the ORCPT parameter including 8-bit UTF-8 characters.

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Address Type
requirements.text: That is, the utf-8-address form MUST NOT be used:

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Address Type
requirements.text: in the ORCPT parameter when the SMTP server doesn't advertise support for SMTPUTF8 (utf-8-addr-xtext MUST be used instead); or

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Address Type
requirements.text: if the SMTP server supports SMTPUTF8, but the address contains ASCII characters not permitted in the ORCPT parameter (e.g., the ORCPT parameter forbids unencoded SP and the '=' character), (either utf-8-addr-unitext or utf-8-addr-xtext MUST be used instead); or

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Address Type
requirements.text: in a 7-bit transport environment including a message/ delivery-status "Original-Recipient:" or "Final-Recipient:" field, (utf-8-addr-xtext MUST be used instead).

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Address Type
requirements.text: The utf-8-address form MAY be used in the ORCPT parameter when the SMTP server also advertises support for SMTPUTF8 and the address doesn't contain any ASCII characters not permitted in the ORCPT parameter.

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Address Type
requirements.text: It SHOULD be used in a message/global-delivery-status "Original-Recipient:" or "Final-Recipient:" DSN field, or in an "Original-Recipient:" header field [RFC3798] if the message is a SMTPUTF8 message.

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Address Type
requirements.text: When sending data to a SMTPUTF8-capable server, native UTF-8 characters SHOULD be used instead of the EmbeddedUnicodeChar syntax described below.

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Address Type
requirements.text: When sending data to an SMTP server that does not advertise SMTPUTF8, then the EmbeddedUnicodeChar syntax MUST be used instead of UTF-8.

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Address Type
requirements.text: When the ORCPT parameter is placed in a message/ global-delivery-status "Original-Recipient:" field, the utf-8-addr-xtext form of the UTF-8 address type SHOULD be converted to the utf-8-address form (see the ABNF below) by removing the unitext encoding.

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Address Type
requirements.text: However, if an address is labeled with the UTF-8 address type but does not conform to utf-8 syntax, then it MUST be copied into the message/global-delivery-status field without alteration.

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Address Type
requirements.text: utf-8-addr-unitext = 1*(QUCHAR / EmbeddedUnicodeChar) ; MUST follow utf-8-address ABNF when ; dequoted.

requirements.heading: The message/global-delivery-status Media Type
requirements.text: First, the charset for message/global-delivery-status is UTF-8, and thus any field MAY contain UTF-8 characters when appropriate (see the ABNF below).

requirements.heading: The message/global-delivery-status Media Type
requirements.text: In particular, the "Diagnostic-Code:" field MAY contain UTF-8 as described in SMTPUTF8 [RFC6531]; the "Diagnostic-Code:" field SHOULD be in i-default language [RFC2277].

requirements.heading: The message/global-delivery-status Media Type
requirements.text: Second, systems generating a message/global-delivery-status body part SHOULD use the utf-8-address

requirements.heading: The message/global-delivery-status Media Type
requirements.text: These systems SHOULD up- convert the utf-8-addr-xtext or the utf-8-addr-unitext form of a UTF-8 address type in the ORCPT parameter to the utf-8-address form of a UTF-8 address type in the "Original-Recipient:" field.

requirements.heading: The message/global-delivery-status Media Type
requirements.text: All instances of "Localized-Diagnostic:" MUST use different language tags.

requirements.heading: Using These Media Types with multipart/report
requirements.text: Note that as far as a multipart/report [RFC6522] container is concerned, message/global-delivery-status, message/global, and message/global-headers MUST be treated as equivalent to message/ delivery-status, message/rfc822, and text/rfc822-headers.

requirements.heading: Using These Media Types with multipart/report
requirements.text: implementations processing multipart/report MUST expect any combinations of the 6 media types mentioned above inside a multipart/ report media type.

requirements.heading: Using These Media Types with multipart/report
requirements.text: (In the event all content is 7-bit, the equivalent traditional types for delivery status notifications MAY be used.

requirements.heading: Additional Requirements on SMTP Servers
requirements.text: If the return-path SMTP server does not support SMTPUTF8, then the undeliverable body part and headers MUST be encoded using a 7-bit Content-Transfer-Encoding such as "base64" or "quoted-printable" [RFC2045], as detailed in Section 4.

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Message Disposition Notifications
requirements.text: First, the charset for message/global-disposition-notification is UTF-8, and thus any field MAY contain UTF-8 characters when appropriate (see the ABNF below).

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Message Disposition Notifications
requirements.text: (In particular, the failure-field, the error-field, and the warning-field MAY contain UTF-8.

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Message Disposition Notifications
requirements.text: These fields SHOULD be in i-default

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Message Disposition Notifications
requirements.text: language [RFC2277].) Second, systems generating a message/ global-disposition-notification body part (typically a mail user agent) SHOULD use the UTF-8 address type for all addresses containing characters outside the ASCII repertoire.

requirements.heading: UTF-8 Message Disposition Notifications
requirements.text: When generating an "Original-Recipient:" header field, a delivery agent writing a UTF-8 header message in native format SHOULD convert the utf-8-addr-xtext or the utf-8-addr-unitext form of a UTF-8 address type in the ORCPT parameter to the corresponding utf-8-address form.

requirements.heading: Update to 'smtp' Diagnostic Type Registration
requirements.text: When the 'smtp' diagnostic type is used in the context of a message/ global-delivery-status body part, the codes remain the same, but the text portion MAY contain UTF-8 characters.

requirements.heading: Update to 'smtp' Diagnostic Type Registration
requirements.text: Whenever possible, the 8-bit content transfer encoding SHOULD be used.

requirements.heading: Update to 'smtp' Diagnostic Type Registration
requirements.text: When this media type passes through a 7-bit-only SMTP infrastructure, it MAY be encoded with the base64 or quoted-printable content transfer encoding.

requirements.heading: Update to 'smtp' Diagnostic Type Registration
requirements.text: As a result, implementations MUST NOT include a charset parameter with this media type.

requirements.heading: Update to 'smtp' Diagnostic Type Registration
requirements.text: The 8-bit content transfer encoding MUST be used with this content-type, unless it is sent over a 7-bit transport environment, in which case quoted- printable or base64 may be necessary.
